_comment: Sounds the owner accepted in the sidecar's P45 ship review. The bytes here are the exact clips the owner marked ok, and they are option 1 in any round for that sound. Sounds on the revisit list are not here - they are still open. THIS FILE IS THE SOUND LEDGER. It once promised that its entries 'become the row in tools/voice-sounds.csv when the sound-out reveal is built'; the reveal shipped on 2026-08-11 and that migration was never finished, so the promise was false for three days and pointed every reader at the wrong master. Corrected 2026-08-14 (open-faults F2). Verdicts live HERE. tools/voice-sounds.csv is the older ledger, it is missing eight sounds that ship, and its 'family' column means a phonetic class where this file's means a render recipe - the same key, opposite meanings, so the two must never be naively merged. tools/ledger-truth.mjs (gate G16b) refuses any disagreement between them.
_revisit_note: No sounds are open. The inventory is complete and entirely synthesised: all 14 sounds that had stood on the owner's own recordings were replaced between rounds 12 and 19 (2026-08-11), on the owner's ruling that no recording of their voice ships.

_ship_review_2026_08_12: Ten shipped sounds re-heard side by side, owner's verdicts. short_a BEST; short_e, short_i, short_o, short_u, schwa, long_e, oo_book good; th_this and h POOR. Two things this closed. First: a verdict does not survive a change of context. th_this and h were both graded 'perfect (owner)' in their own rounds and are poor when heard beside their neighbours, so a sound must be judged in the company it will keep, not alone. Second: the owner ruled the same day that schwa 'was the one I think we did the least well' and must not be used as the authority for making new sounds - it had been the target of three failed rounds for the word 'a'. short_a is the reference now, and its entry records no method at all, which is its own fault (docs/open-faults.md).

It is a SECOND schwa on the owner's ruling that the schwa inside "the" stays as it is; the two are different recordings, 360 ms against 150.

v_soft.how: a buzzing v, quieter and rounder - the v of “of” only
v_soft.note: SND16's v re-cut after the owner called it shouting beside the vowel in “of”: measured 6.2 dB louder and 400 Hz brighter than the sound next to it. Recipe, from the shipped d:v's own body: gain -7 dB, one-pole low-pass at 1800 Hz, re-peaked to -3.5 dBFS, 40 ms fades, then the pack's 80/300 ms padding. ONLY “of” takes it. van, vet, vat and vex keep d:v, which was graded perfect for them in SND16 and sits within 0.7 dB of its neighbours there. Reproduce with tools/build_of_round.py --ship, which refuses unless the source and the result both hash to the values recorded here.
